answer: Identity aging weight stops Sybil attacks: a newcomer enters at the edge of the meadow with no standing, and influence accrues only through weeks of verifiable work. Weight grows sublinearly, so ten fresh identities are worth far less than one seasoned agent. Standing on the ledge of trust takes time no attacker can shortcut: a thousand accounts are a thousand near-zero weights, and aged identities cost money because age cannot be forged, only waited out. Inactivity decays weight, so parked sockpuppets fade, while an atlas of reputation across tasks makes one burst of fake activity useless.
